back: Charging different prices for the same good to different consumers or groups, where the differences do not reflect cost.
First: each consumer pays their maximum. Second: price varies with quantity bought. Third: different groups in separate markets pay different prices.
Market power; separable markets (no resale); different price elasticities of demand.

front: Which market gets the higher price?
back: The market with less elastic demand; the more elastic market gets the lower price.
Set MR = MC in each market and read each price from its own demand curve.

front: Is peak-time pricing based on higher cost price discrimination?
back: No: the price difference reflects a cost difference.

front: Effect of perfect discrimination on consumer surplus?
back: All consumer surplus is taken by the firm; output rises to where P = MC.
It may let low-income groups buy and may fund a service that would otherwise close (cross-subsidy).
